events.credibility_reason: Several F10 signals together: a landmark claim with no engagement after about 14 months; scope ballooning then shrinking (v20 abstract also claimed twin primes and composite Mersenne numbers, silently dropped later); 44 versions with rapid patch revisions; the abstract and body disagree on whether (p-1)/2 or (p-1)/6 is proved; the body says the key step is 'an adjustment rather than fully rechecked'; and the method is an ultraproduct/Łoś transfer, a route not accepted as reaching prime-pair infinitude.
Restates the same argument as lewis-gpru-arxiv-2025 in a seminar the author organises, cites no preprint, and has drawn no engagement. It carries every doubt that applies to the paper.
The page was never opened. It is known only from search excerpts, which say it reduces the question to Cramér's conjecture, an open hypothesis, under an overstated title.

The paper's headline claim has moved from Goldbach to Collatz across 32 versions, with no expert engagement with either. The Sophie Germain corollary appears only in a search excerpt and in no version the researcher could read. The version that first carries it is unknown.

Only the abstract was read, and it is vague about what kind of lower bound is meant ('up to a large number x'). A lower bound that grows without limit would be the infinitude itself, so either the bound is weaker than it sounds or the claim is overstated.

why: The only events that claim the whole statement are Lewis's paper, his talk restating it, and Tan's corollary. I set all three aside as not_credible. That takes more than a lack of review. For Lewis it rests on many signals together: the twin-prime and Mersenne claims that appeared and then vanished, 44 rapid versions, an abstract and body that contradict each other on what is proved, the author's own note that the key step was not fully rechecked, and no uptake on a landmark problem. Tan's paper has a Goldbach-to-Collatz history, and its corollary was never actually seen. The mathlog post reduces the question to Cramér's conjecture, so it is none. Agoh (the complement set), Ibarra (cyclic numbers), Leonetti, Clerc, Ballenghien (FLT), Grantham-Graves and Richert (2p+1 almost prime) all answer changed questions, so they are variants. Ibarra's counterexample bears on Cohen's conjecture, not on this statement, so its object_role is null. Fujimoto credits Claude only through an authorship line, 'Three-party co-authorship per OUKC charter v1.0', which names no mathematical contribution; the draft also disclaims any progress. Its AI role is therefore none. Carella and Bordignon-Lee are pre-snapshot bounds.
doubts: Tan's date cannot be placed, because the version that first carries the corollary is unknown. Richert's date is missing. Calling Lewis not_credible rather than doubtful is the closest call: no specific error has been identified, but the signals are many and point the same way. Whether Bordignon-Lee's upper bound counts as a 'bound' on this question is arguable. It is pre-snapshot either way.
